methodology_note: Each probe reuses an existing fixed-frequency divider testbench schematic (NSEL strapped statically for its N, open loop: no VCO, PFD/charge pump or loop filter), netlists it once per modulus, and rewrites only the CLK pulse source and the RESETB pwl source per probe from the single probe frequency. The declared waveform assumptions are: ideal rail-to-rail CLK whose high level tracks each point's own supply (the fixed-frequency records hold it at 1.8 V regardless of supply), 12.5 ps rise and fall, 50% duty at the 50% points, RESETB low until 5 ns and ramping to the supply by 6 ns, NSEL static. Modulus: only N=20 is declared here; N=20 is the ratio of the proposed 500 MHz interface and no adjacent modulus is claimed to stand in for it. The 500 MHz probe is declared in `mandatory_probes_hz`: the driver schedules it in stage 1 of every cell in addition to the coarse probes and reports its verdict apart from the boundary, so it is neither inferred from an Fmax boundary nor dependent on being among the coarse probes (with a 400 MHz floor, 25 MHz resolution and stride 8 the coarse probes are 400, 600, ..., 2600 MHz and 500 MHz is not one of them). An INCONCLUSIVE mandatory probe (simulator trouble, missing or truncated waveform) is an invalid run and is reported as such, distinct from an electrical FAIL (a completed waveform missing the per-period criterion); neither is a passing capability claim.
analysis: transient per probe (`tran 10p <stop>`, injected by the Fmax driver); stop = reset release + (skip + min_periods + margin) expected output periods, so the window scales with N and the probe frequency. Search is a two-stage grid search on the declared resolution grid: stage 1 probes every coarse_stride-th grid point (plus the top of the range); stage 2 probes every grid point strictly inside the lowest coarse pass-to-fail transition. A pass island hidden between two coarse probes would be missed and is a stated limitation.
